mina: quick note — int4 bring-up for the new 4B candidate produced two unexpected effects on our multilingual suite :eyes:
mina: 1) short CJK queries (<8 tokens) have much worse retrieval embedding cosine (avg -0.11). 2) ja->ko translation BLEU down ~3.8 on small devset, with a recurring doubled-jamo merge in outputs.

kai: can you paste the eval summary? which evals exactly?
eval-bot: eval-run: r-2026-03-15-09, model: rwin-4b-v1-int4, evals: retrieval_short_queries, mt_ja_ko_dev.
eval-bot: retrieval_short_queries: mean_cosine=0.72 (baseline fp16=0.83), p@10 drop 12%.
eval-bot: mt_ja_ko_dev: BLEU=21.4 (baseline fp16=25.2), chrF down 2.7.
mina: attaching minimal repro log excerpt below — this is from local quantized run with our int4 kernel set and streaming+kvcache enabled:
```
# repro cmd
python -m eval.run --model rwin-4b-v1 --quantize int4 --quant-kernel gptq-llm --use-streaming --kv-cache --eval mt_ja_ko_dev,retrieval_short_queries --batch 8
```
```
# tokenizer merge diffs (token->merged_subtoken) sampled from failing cases
'ᄒ' + 'ᅡ' -> '하'  # expected
'ᄒ' + 'ᅡ' + 'ᅵ' -> '하이'  # sometimes becomes two tokens (ハイ-like) or duplicated jamo
'ㅂ' + 'ㅏ' -> '바'  # OK
'ㄱ' + 'ㅏ' -> '가가'  # REGRESSION: duplicated merge appears in ~30% of failing outputs
```
mina: full log attached in s3 (s3://redwood-dev/evals/2147501122/r-2026-03-15-09.log) — but the short repro is above.

jun: is this only on int4? any int8 or fp16 runs?
mina: int8 fp16 both match baseline (no dup merges). int4 with gptq-llm kernel only. tried two different random seeds, reproducible.
kai: hypothesis: the quantized embedding table may have changed indices for particular multibyte subwords (sentencepiece/token id remap) or our post-quant bias folding interacts with kv cache streaming ordering.
mina: i diffed tokenizer json between fp16 and quantized runtime — config bytes identical. but index->subtoken mapping in the runtime lookup table dump shows a few indices remapped (likely during kernel packing).

jun: can you dump the packed embedding indices and a tiny repro to confirm? also try disabling kv-cache or streaming (should be fast) to see if it's purely quant kernel ordering.
mina: did that:
```
# quick checks
python -c "from runtime import packed_table; print(packed_table[100:130])"  # shows shifted ids
# disable kv
python -m eval.run --model rwin-4b-v1 --quantize int4 --quant-kernel gptq-llm --no-kv-cache --no-streaming --eval mt_ja_ko_dev --batch 8
```
mina: with --no-kv-cache BLEU returns to 24.8 (much closer), and duplicated merges disappear in outputs. retrieval cosine also recovers ~+0.07.

kai: that points to an ordering/race between packed embedding reads and kvcache offsets when using that kernel's packed layout. probably an addressing bug in the kernel read/write offsets for multibyte codepoint fragments.
ops-bot: FYI deploys: dedicated pool rwin-4b-int4-gptq is currently serving canary traffic 1/100 — routed by model tag 'rwin-4b-v1-int4'.
jun: schedule: i can bisect kernels tomorrow. two quick asks: (1) dump packed_table for both kernels (gptq-llm and qlinear) side-by-side, (2) get a tiny failing example (input + model output) and tokenized ids for that exact run. anyone can paste one?
mina: pasted a minimal failing example below (input shortened):
```
# input
日本語の短い問い合わせ: "오늘 날씨 어때"
# token ids (runtime dump): [502, 12413, 301, 97, 128, 11, 9012, 42]
# output (int4,gptq-llm,with-kv): "오늘 가가 날씨 어때요?"  <-- duplicated syllable '가가' before '날씨'
# output (fp16): "오늘가 날씨 어때요?"  <-- expected single '가'
```
jun: perfect. i'll run kernel-level memory-checks and an address-alignment stress test. if it's a packing offset bug we should see consistent index shifts under streaming.
kai: also add a small eval that measures embed cosine specifically for 1-4 token CJK queries — helps us track during kernel patches.
mina: created ticket INF-4567 and linked logs + evals. i'm going to rollback canary to qlinear kernel until we have a patch. ops-bot: rollback scheduled in 5m. :thumbsup:
mina: thanks — will follow up with bisect results and a short writeup. :face_with_thermometer:
jun: thx, will ping once i have kernel trace.
mina: fyi we should add a short test to the onboarding checklist: "run short CJK retrieval/mt smoke with kvcache on int4 kernels" — catches this earlier next time.
kai: agreed.
mina: end.
